title: Oracle Database
text:
In 2024, Oracle renamed the long-term Oracle Database 23c release as Oracle Database 23ai, a change independent coverage attributed to the addition of features for AI-oriented application development.[1] Oracle AI Database 26ai introduced capabilities for agentic AI use cases, including Select AI Agent, AI Private Agent Factory, and an MCP server for Oracle Database integrated with SQLcl. Oracle AI Database 26ai architecture uses a Unified Memory Core, in which multiple data types are processed within a single transactional engine.[2]

Vector search in Oracle AI Database is provided by AI Vector Search, introduced with the 23c/23ai; it adds a native vector data type, vector indexes, and vector-search SQL operators. These features allow semantic representations of documents, images, and other unstructured data to be stored as vectors and used for similarity search in Oracle Database.[3,1] Coverage of the 23ai release also described AI Vector Search as supporting retrieval-augmented generation, a technique that combines large language models with private business data to answer natural-language questions.[3]

In March 2026, Oracle announced the limited availability of Oracle Autonomous AI Vector Database, a fully managed service built on Autonomous AI Database. It provides Python, REST, and PL/SQL interfaces for vector search and supporting semantic search, retrieval-augmented generation and agent-based applications. The service supports vector and metadata filtering, HNSW and IVF indexes. AI Vector Search can support retrieval-augmented generation by retrieving semantically similar content for inclusion in a language-model prompt. Agentic RAG extends retrieval-augmented generation by allowing an AI agent to perform iterative retrieval or tool-use steps while constructing a response. Hybrid search combines vector similarity with lexical search or metadata filters.[4]

In August 2026, Oracle published the VecDB Python SDK for vector search, semantic search, RAG and AI agents on Oracle AI Database 23.26.3 and above with ORDS 26.2.2 and above.[5]

Select AI is a natural-language interface for querying data in Oracle AI Database. Independent coverage described the feature as allowing users to query data in natural language and use large language models to generate SQL for those questions.[3,2] In 26ai, Select AI Agent extended this approach into a framework for building, deploying, and managing agents that can use database functions and knowledge context.[2]

Oracle has also added support for the Model Context Protocol (MCP) through an MCP server for Oracle Database, integrated with SQLcl. InfoWorld described the server as allowing developers to build AI agents that can query, retrieve, and reason over enterprise data in Oracle Databases without custom integration layers.[6] The 26ai release also added AI Private Agent Factory, described in third-party coverage as a framework for deploying private, containerized agents in controlled environments.[2]

The database also includes older in-database machine-learning and data-mining capabilities. Predictive Analytics Using Oracle Data Miner describes Oracle Data Miner and Oracle Data Mining as supporting models such as association rules, classification, clustering, regression, and anomaly detection, with models built and used through SQL and PL/SQL packages.[7] A later Apress book describes the Oracle Machine Learning platform as including OML4SQL, OML Notebooks, OML4R, and OML4Py for developing and deploying machine-learning models with Oracle Database and Autonomous Database.[8]
